newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch -March 5.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch -March 5.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Wednesday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:

** Microsoft Corp chairman Bill Gates said on Tuesday that India had the potential to become a computer software superpower and promised help to New Delhi in building its vital communications infrastructure.
"To be a leader in the digital economy of the 21st
century, India must invest in basic infrastructure, education and information technology," Gates, who arrived on Monday on a four-day visit, said in a speech on information technology.
"These are the tools which will drive the country into
the future and make India an economic and software superpower."
Gates, whose visit was celebrated with lead stories in
newspapers, said he discussed India's need for an information infrastructure, especially in telecommunications, with Prime Minister H. D.Deve Gowda over breakfast on Tuesday.
** International Monetary Fund managing director Michel Camdessus said on Tuesday that his initial impression of India's 1997/98 (April-March) budget was extremely positive.
Asked to comment on the government's tax and spending
plan which was announced last Friday, Camdessus told reporters as he arrived in the Indian capital: "My first impression is extremely positive."
"It is positive because all the people in this country,
in the business community tell me this will help them to do better and contribute better to the overall prosperity of the country," the IMF head said.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram unveiled the budget to
Parliament last week.
** The government has conceded a major relief to hundred percent export-oriented units and those set up in export processing and free trade zones, the Financial Express says.
These units can now sell finished products, waste or
scrap made wholly of indigenous raw materials in the domestic tariff area by paying excise duty only.

** American transnationals operating in India would reap tax benefits in the United States following the recommendation of the expert panel on the Companies Act to retain legal provisions for unlimited companies, the Business Standard reports.
U.S. laws provide a three percent tax shield on profits
earned from investments abroad.
MARKETS:
** The 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange rose 73.56 points, or 1.90 percent, to end at 3,944.61.
** The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index gained 9.6 points, to 1,117.30.
** The Delhi share index rose 13.32 points to 837.05.
-- Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
